chunks: Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā from Muhammad ibn Mūsā from Sahl from Muhammad al-Ṭabarī said:

I wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), asking him about a fish called al-Iblāmī, and a fish called al-Ṭabarānī, and a fish called al-᭤imr, and my companions were forbidding me from eating it. He replied, 'Eat it, there is no harm in it.' I wrote [this reply] in my own handwriting.

key_terms.اَلطَّبَرَانِيُّ: A specific type of fish mentioned in the hadith.
key_terms.اَلطِّمْرُ: A specific type of fish mentioned in the hadith.
key_terms.اَلْإِبْلَامِيُّ: A specific type of fish mentioned in the hadith.
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (a common legal phrase indicating permissibility or lack of objection).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating specific local fish varieties in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Imam’s practical approach to dietary laws, affirming the permissibility of specific regional fish varieties despite local companions' caution. The explicit mention that the reply was 'written in his own hand' (*bi-khathti*) underscores the authenticity and direct authority of the Imam’s ruling in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the principle that unless a specific prohibition is established, aquatic creatures are generally permissible (*mubah*).
